newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Text of Canada's letter to the United Nations.
newsitem.headline: Text of Canada's letter to the United Nations.

text.p: Following is the text of a letter to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali from Canada's U.N. ambassador, Robert Fowler, circulated to Security Council members late on Thursday. It explains the purpose of the mission to eastern Zaire and was required before the 15-seat council could authorise the force, expected on Friday:

"The humanitarian situation in eastern Zaire continues to deteriorate. In particular, the plight of refugees and displaced persons in that region remains desperate while efforts by international humanitarian agencies to reach those in need continue to be impeded. Hundreds of thousands of lives are at risk, with many thousands liable to die in the absence of immediate relief. Action by the international community is required now to avoid a humanitarian catastrophe.

"Security Council resolution 1078 urges member states on an urgent and temporary basis in cooperation with the Secretary-General and with the OAU (Organization of African Unity) to prepare the necessary arrangements, in consultation with the states concerned, to facilitate the immediate return of humanitarian organisations and the effective delivery by civilian relief organisations of humanitarian aid to alleviate the immediate suffering of displaced persons, refugees and civilians at risk in eastern Zaire, and to facilitate the voluntary, orderly repatriation of refugees by UNHCR (the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees) and the voluntary return of displaced persons. We envisage, as a legal framework for this intervention, a resolution under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations providing for a mandate to act.

To this end, the Prime Minister of Canada and other Canadian authorities have consulted with a number of governments, including those in the region. In our judgment, the international will now exists for the formation of a multinational operation. The Government of Canada is prepared to work without delay with other governments to enable the deployment of a temporary humanitarian operation for eastern Zaire. We have secured the agreement of a number of member states to participate in such an operation. We are also in contact with the OAU. Canada would be ready to take the lead in organising and commanding such an operation. The objectives assigned to that operation would be consistent with the ones outlined in resolution 1078, as stated in the preceding paragraph. These are humanitarian objectives, which are not intended to interfere with the balance of military forces in the area nor to support the re-establishment of camps in which armed elements are able to operate.

"As we see it, this temporary humanitarian operation should terminate on 31 March, 1997, unless the Security Council, on the basis of a report of the Secretary-General, determines that the objectives of the operation have been fulfilled earlier. Within that timeframe, and as soon as possible, the Security Council should authorise the deployment of a follow-on operation on the basis of recommendations by the Secretary-General. This would succeed the temporary multinational force. In this regard, we believe it would be appropriate for you to send an advance team to eastern Zaire with the purpose of reporting to you on the requirements for this follow-on operation and for the transition from the multinational force.
"I should be grateful if you would have this letter circulated as a Security Council document."
